new_finding: BPS September 2024 Susenas data (confirmed via multiple independent secondary citations) gives: affluent = 1.29M persons (~380K HH); BPS middle class = 48.41M persons. The claim's '7-9M combined affluent + upper-middle' requires the 'upper-middle' sub-band to be ~5.7-7.7M persons (12-16% of BPS middle class). BPS does not publish this sub-band separately — the [ASSUMED-3] tag is correct and necessary. Household arithmetic using avg HH size 3.4 yields affluent HH ~380K (not 330K as stated in current evidence) and implied upper-middle HH of 1.4-1.9M, putting combined HH range at roughly 1.8-2.3M — consistent with the claim but the upper-middle band remains [ASSUMED]. CRITICAL DISCREPANCY on Tier-1 concentration: east.vc/Jakarta Post citing East Ventures DCI 2024 report states ~70% of Indonesia's population lives in Tier-2/3 cities, implying ~30% in Tier-1 — directly contradicting the claim's 55-65% Tier-1 concentration. No primary BPS or World Bank source found for the 55-65% figure. The BPS October 2024 primary page (bps.go.id/en/news/2024/10/25/622) returns 403.
